BlogPost.title: BlogPost
BlogPost.description: Represents a blog post on the website.

id.description: Unique identifier for the blog post.

content.description: The main content of the blog post, likely in HTML or Markdown format.

author.description: Name of the author of the blog post.

datePublished.description: Date and time when the blog post was published.

tags.description: Tags associated with the blog post.

imageUrl.description: URL to the main image of the blog post, optimized for different display sizes.

summary.description: A brief summary or excerpt of the blog post.

definition.description: Stores blog posts that admin can create. Includes all blog post data.

params.name: blogPostId
params.description: Unique identifier for the blog post.

definition.description: Documents in this collection indicate admin privileges. Existence of a document with a specific uid grants admin access. There is no schema in this collection since its presense is all that matters.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user.

firestore.reasoning:
The data structure prioritizes simplicity and security for managing blog posts. Since only admins should be able to upload blog posts, a dedicated collection `blogPosts` is used. An alternative would be using a subcollection under a user document, but considering the user case it is recommended to use only one `blogPosts` collection.

**Authorization Independence:**
The structure relies on the absence of hierarchical dependencies. No `get()` calls are required in security rules to validate access to blog posts.

**QAPs Support:**
*   **List Operation Security:** List operations are secured by checking the user's admin role in the `roles_admin` collection, ensuring only admins can read the collection.
